purpose: Exploratory fixed-transect Earth/Moon terrain-obstruction comparison, not analog-site validation
sampling: Earth exported profile retained. Lunar 5m cells averaged in 6x6 blocks, bilinearly sampled at the same 83 distances. Both elevation models have approximately 30m grid spacing; effective resolutions and errors differ. No vertical rescaling.
uncertainty_method: Maximum native RMS in each 6x6 block, then maximum of four coarse neighboring cells at profile sample. This upper proxy avoids an unjustified independence assumption. Two-RMS sensitivity envelope sums terrain and endpoint RMS proxies with interpolation weights; it is not a confidence interval or guaranteed error bound.
selection: Illustrative western-rim lines at y=-6000,-6500,-7000m, x=-4000m to -4000+L. Center line is primary. No optimization against Earth data. Not representative of the full Moon or all of Shackleton rim.
physics: 2m base/rover antennas. 5m trial relay at highest sampled terrain point. Local spherical-curvature approximation included separately for Earth/Moon. No atmospheric refraction, Fresnel-zone clearance, RF propagation, buildings or subgrid obstacles.
limits: Earth vertical uncertainty was not supplied and has not been propagated.
Reported lunar RMS does not capture every possible systematic or model error.
Resampling to equal pixel spacing does not equalize effective resolution.
Comparisons apply to these fixed trial lines. They neither validate nor reject Kilbourne Hole as a whole.
Peak placement is a trial strategy, not an optimized network.
Earth and Moon coordinates must remain in separate QGIS projects; do not transform one planet into the other.
